asset: Comet Cruise sprites: the rocket, a star, a space rock
generation_log: art/scratch/generation-log.jsonl in the main checkout, lines 1028 and 1029 (two sheets) and 1030 (the edit)
open_sources: Openverse, CC0 images, 2026-10-18: "cute rocket star sprite watercolor" found nothing.
references: art/source/moles/moles-sheet-raw.png (the moles' sheet, for its style)
prompt_summary: Eight watercolor-and-ink sprites in four columns and two rows on flat magenta: a cream rocket with a red nose cone and fins, a sky-blue porthole, and a small flame, straight, tilted left, tilted right, and wobbling with motion lines and tiny circling stars; a plump golden star; a burst of golden sparkles; a lumpy warm-grey cratered space rock; a soft puff of pale cream dust.
key_colour: #FF00FF magenta, absent from the sprites' palette
post_processing: Two sheets; sheet A (line 1029, kept as art/source/arcade/comet-sprites-before-edit-raw.png) selected after a visual review: the brief's small flame and clearer wobble lines.

Its star's soft glow was painted over the magenta and came out pink, which keying can't separate; one edit (line 1030) took the glow away and left the rest of the sheet as it was (other cells' mean difference 2 to 4 levels). That edit is the source. A glow, if wanted, is drawn in code.

tools/art/build-comet-sprites.ts keys each cell's magenta at 22% fuzz like the moles, takes the spill off the 3px alpha-edge band only (despill-edge.ts), trims, scales all eight by one factor so the rocket keeps its size in every pose, and centres them in 256px frames of a 1024x512 atlas with centre anchors.
Left as painted: a faint 1 to 2 px pink edge on parts of the star, visible only magnified (the reviewer called it unobtrusive at game size), and the rocket fins' dark crimson outline.
Rebuilt twice with identical output hash.

owner_review.note: For the owner: the rocket, the star, the rock, and their sparkle and puff.
